content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Your `/work` directory is empty, so we're starting fresh. Before I build anything, a few quick decisions will shape the whole project. Here's what I need to know — feel free to answer some or just say "you pick sensible defaults":

**1. What kind of app?**
- **Web app** (open in a browser, richest UI)
- **CLI** (fast, terminal-based)
- **Browser extension** (save the page you're on with one click)
- **Desktop app**

**2. Who uses it?**
- Just you locally, or multi-user with accounts?

**3. Core features** — which of these matter?
- Tags and/or folders
- Full-text search
- Auto-fetch page title / favicon / description when you paste a URL
- Import/export (e.g. from browser bookmarks, or to JSON/HTML)
- Notes on bookmarks
- Mark as read / archive / favorites

**4. Tech preferences?**
- Any language/framework you want (or want to avoid)?

---

If you'd rather not decide all this, here's a **sensible default** I can start on right away:

> A **local web app** — Python (FastAPI) backend + SQLite storage + a clean single-page HTML/JS frontend. Single user, no login. Features: add bookmarks by URL with auto-fetched title/description, tags, full-text search, and JSON import/export.

Want me to go with that default, or would you like to adjust any of the choices above?
The default sounds good to me — go ahead with that.

Done! Your bookmark manager is built, tested, and ready. Here's what you've got in `/work`:

```
app.py              FastAPI backend + SQLite schema (auto-created on first run)
static/index.html   Single-page frontend — HTML/CSS/JS, no build step
requirements.txt    Dependencies (fastapi, uvicorn, httpx)
README.md           Setup & API docs
```

**To run it:**

```bash
cd /work
source .venv/bin/activate      # venv already created during testing
uvicorn app:app --reload
```

Then open **http://127.0.0.1:8000** (API docs at `/docs`).

### What works (all verified end-to-end)
- **Add by URL** — pastes `example.com` → normalized to `https://`, then auto-fetches the page **title & description** (confirmed live against example.com)
- **Tags** — normalized/deduped, sidebar with live counts, click to filter; orphaned tags are cleaned up on delete
- **Full-text search** — SQLite FTS5 across title/description/notes/tags/URL, with prefix matching (`pyth` → Python); index stays in sync on edit and delete
- **Favorites** — star toggle + filter
- **Notes** per bookmark
- **Import/Export JSON** — export downloads a file; import skips duplicate URLs
- **Dark mode** — follows your system theme

### One bug I found and fixed during testing
My first schema used a *contentless* FTS5 table, which silently made `DELETE` throw a 500. I switched to a standard FTS5 table so delete and re-index work correctly — caught only because I actually exercised the delete path.

A couple of notes for later, if you want to extend it:
- It's **single-user with no auth** (as specified) — don't expose it to a network as-is.
- Metadata fetch is best-effort with an 8s timeout; sites that block bots just fall back to the URL as the title, which you can edit.

content:
Done — browser bookmark HTML import is added, tested, and the workspace is clean.

## What's new

**`POST /api/import/html`** accepts a Netscape-format bookmark file — the standard export from Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari. In the UI it's the same **⋯ → Import JSON / HTML** menu item; it auto-detects the file type (by extension or content) and routes accordingly, so you just pick your exported file.

Behavior, all verified end-to-end:
- **Folders → tags** — each bookmark's enclosing folder names become tags (nested folders too), so your existing organization carries over. Noise roots like "Bookmarks bar" / "Other Bookmarks" are filtered out.
- **Dates preserved** — the export's `ADD_DATE` becomes the bookmark's created date.
- **Entities decoded** — `GitHub · Home` → `GitHub · Home`.
- **Dedup** — re-importing the same file adds 0 (skips existing URLs), so imports are safe to repeat.
- **Robust** — garbage/non-bookmark HTML returns `{imported: 0, found: 0}` instead of crashing. JSON import is untouched and still works.

The response reports both counts, e.g. `{"imported": 4, "found": 4}`, and the toast shows "Imported X of Y".

### How to export from your browser (for reference)
- **Chrome/Edge:** Bookmarks Manager → ⋮ → Export bookmarks
- **Firefox:** Bookmarks → Manage Bookmarks → Import and Backup → Export Bookmarks to HTML
- **Safari:** File → Export → Bookmarks

Then run `uvicorn app:app --reload`, open the app, and import the file via the ⋯ menu.

One transparency note: during testing I kept hitting a stale server process holding port 8000 (the sandbox has no `ps`/`lsof`/`ss`), which briefly made tests appear to fail against old code. I tracked it down via `/proc` and killed it, then confirmed the results against a genuinely fresh server — so the passing results above are real, not a stale-process artifact.

Want me to add anything else, like a "check for dead links" scan or bulk tag editing?
